Source: Jackson et al., Toxins, 2016; Lee et al., 2016
texto_aprovado: Elapids seem to have been the first venomous snakes to reach the continent. And notice who wasn't there. Australia had no vipers, the family of rattlesnakes, and none of the other modern snake families had arrived. In Australia, elapids fill most of the roles a snake can play on land, and some live in the sea. The inland taipan is one of them.
